Cross-validation results

Source: R/doc_cv_class.R
multiScaleR_cv-class.Rd

The cross-validation functions return a list of class multiScaleR_cv. This page describes every element of that list, what each score measures and on what scale, and which functions read the result. Several functions add a subclass that changes or adds a few elements, and those differences are described at the end.

Which functions return it

FunctionClass of the result
cross_validate(), cross_validate_glm() (Gaussian, Poisson, binomial)multiScaleR_cv
cross_validate(), cross_validate_glm() ("nbinom2", "Gamma")multiScaleR_distribution_cv, multiScaleR_cv
cross_validate_clogit()multiScaleR_choice_cv, multiScaleR_cv
cross_validate_field()multiScaleR_field_cv, multiScaleR_cv
cross_validate_mixed()multiScaleR_mixed_cv, multiScaleR_cv
cross_validate_bayes()multiScaleR_bayes_cv, multiScaleR_cv
select_cv()the class of its candidates

A fold is one split of the data into analysis rows, which fit the model, and assessment rows, which are held out and scored. An assessment occurrence is one held-out row in one fold. A row assessed in two folds has two occurrences.

Read these elements first

  • complete: TRUE when every planned fold was fitted and scored. When any fold fails it is FALSE, and every pooled score in summary is NA. Never rank a model on the folds that happened to finish.

  • summary: data frame of pooled scores, one row per metric.

    • metric names the score, and estimate is the pooled score (lower is better).

    • unit says what one score refers to, "observation" or, for the Brier score, "trial".

    • n_assessment is the number of planned assessment occurrences, and n_scored the number that entered the score.

    • weight_sum is the total frequency weight behind the score (frequency weight x trials for the Brier score).

    • complete repeats the completion flag.

  • metrics: the same columns plus fold, with one row per fold and metric. A fold that finished keeps its scores even when another fold failed. The pooled RMSE is not the mean of the fold RMSEs.

  • fold_results: data frame with fold, n_analysis and n_assessment (rows used to fit and to score), and status, either "scored" or "failed".

  • errors: list with one element per fold. It is NULL for a scored fold. For a failed fold it holds stage, where the fold stopped (for example "initial_glm", "scale_fit", "prediction", or "training_selection" in a select_cv() result), and message, the reason. A failed scale fit can also carry start_results or radius_profile. Failed folds are never retried.

  • warnings: list with one character vector per fold, holding the warning messages captured while that fold was fitted and predicted. They are captured rather than printed, so read them here.

Read the scores

Every score is a loss, so lower is better. Each assessment occurrence gets its own loss, stored in a column of predictions named after the metric. The pooled estimate is the frequency-weighted mean of those losses over the eligible occurrences. An occurrence is eligible when its frequency weight is positive and, for binomial data, it has at least one trial. Ineligible occurrences stay in predictions with eligible = FALSE and contribute nothing.

MetricLoss for one occurrencePooled score and its scale
rmseSquared error, (observed - predicted)^2Square root of the mean squared error, in response units (for example, animals per survey)
maeAbsolute errorMean absolute error, in response units
neg_log_scoreNegative natural log of the probability (counts, binomial successes) or density (Gamma) that the fitted model gives the observed valueMean per observation, in natural-log units
deviancePoisson deviance contribution (Poisson only)Mean per observation
brierSquared error of the success probability, averaged over the row's trials (binomial only)Mean per trial, between 0 and 1

How to read the scores

  • RMSE and MAE judge only the predicted mean. RMSE weighs large misses heavily, and MAE treats every miss in proportion to its size. Note that the rmse column of predictions holds squared errors, not their roots.

  • The negative log score judges the whole predicted distribution, so it also penalizes a model that is too confident. It keeps every constant of the probability function, such as the binomial coefficient. A difference of D between two models means the better one gave the observed outcomes exp(D) times the probability, as a geometric mean per observation. A difference of 0.1 is a ratio of about 1.11. For Gamma responses the score is a density, so it depends on the response units and can be negative.

  • An observed outcome given zero probability produces an infinite log score. The value is kept, not clipped.

  • For NB2 and Gamma, the log score uses theta or the dispersion estimated from the analysis rows and frozen for scoring.

  • A score means little alone. Compare candidates fitted to the same folds with cv_tab().

Other elements

  • predictions: data frame with one row per assessment occurrence, including the occurrences of failed folds, whose predictions and losses are NA.

    • fold and row_id identify the occurrence.

    • observed is the response (the number of successes for binomial data), and trials is 1 except for cbind(successes, failures) responses.

    • prediction is the expected response on the response scale (the mean count, the mean, or the probability of success per trial).

    • weight is the frequency weight, and eligible marks the occurrences that enter the scores.

    • One loss column per metric is named after the metric.

    • NB2 and Gamma results add distribution_family, the frozen training theta (NB2) or dispersion (Gamma), with NA where it does not apply, and poisson_limit, which is TRUE only when a joint NB2 fit verified the exact Poisson limit.

  • training: list with one element per fold, describing the fits to the analysis rows. An element can be empty or partial when its fold failed early.

    • coefficients: final regression coefficients on the link scale (log for Poisson, NB2, and Gamma, logit for binomial, identity for Gaussian). Use exp() on a log-link coefficient for a multiplicative change in the expected response. Spatial covariates are standardized with the training mean and SD, so their coefficients refer to a one training SD change, unless covariate_transform = "raw" was used.

    • initial_coefficients: coefficients of the initial GLM, fitted at the starting scales.

    • scale_est: data frame with Mean and SE, the estimated sigma and its standard error in map units, one row per optimized covariate. Similar values across folds suggest that the data identify the scales well.

    • shape_est: estimated kernel shape (unitless) for kernels that have one, otherwise NULL.

    • initial_normalization, fitted_normalization: lists of mean and sd, the analysis-row centering and scaling of each spatial covariate at the starting and the fitted scales. Assessment rows reuse them.

    • bin_reference: the frozen distance bins (breaks, representative distances bin_rep, the extraction envelope domain, and cell_size). Distances are in units of max_D, so 1 equals max_D.

    • optimizer: par (the optimized scale parameters on the internal scale, sigma divided by max_D), value (the minimized objective), convergence (0 means success), and message.

    • start_results: the table of optimizer starts from multiScale_optim(), when available.

    • initial_distribution (NB2 and Gamma): the nuisance parameter of the initial fit, in the same form as distribution.

    cross_validate_glm() estimates no scales, so its training holds only coefficients (plus the NB2 and Gamma items).

  • distribution (NB2 and Gamma only): list with one element per fold, holding the frozen training distribution. An element is NULL when the training fit failed.

    • family, with theta (the NB2 size, Inf only for a verified Poisson limit) or dispersion (the Gamma dispersion).

    • poisson_limit, and estimated, which is FALSE when the parameter was fixed in advance.

    • convention, how the value was obtained, for example "native_gamma_deviance_scale" (the training deviance divided by the sum of the weights).

    • rank, native_K, logLik, nobs, training_deviance, and sum_weights of the training fit.

  • diagnostics: list with one element per fold. initial_glm and fitted_glm hold converged, boundary, and iter from the initial and final GLM (NB2 and Gamma results also record th.warn and SE.theta where the native fit has them). scale holds the scale-fit diagnostics described in diagnostics(). Check them before ranking models, because a scored fold is not necessarily a trustworthy one.

  • prediction_contracts: list of the prediction contracts attached by the prediction method of each fold (see prediction_contract). Each states what the prediction conditions on and which uncertainty it leaves out. It can be empty when the prediction method attaches none.

  • folds: the split plan as supplied.

  • assessment_counts: named integer vector, one value per input row, giving how many times the row was assessed (0 for rows never held out).

  • targets: data frame with row_id, observed, trials, and weight for every row used in any split, sorted by row ID. cv_tab() and select_cv() use it to confirm that candidates were scored on the same data. It never enters a fit.

  • selection_records: NULL unless keep_selection = TRUE. Otherwise a list with one compact record per fold, read by select_cv(). Each record holds version, controls, diagnostics, metadata warnings, data, and an error message if the record could not be built. Leave the records unchanged. They cannot rebuild the fitted models. A successful data holds these items.

    • logLik, the training log-likelihood (natural log).

    • native_K, the parameter count of the fitted regression as its log-likelihood reports it, including an estimated dispersion or theta.

    • ecological_K, the number of estimated scales and shapes, and K, their total.

    • nobs and observation_ids, the rows that entered the likelihood.

    • targets, the analysis-row responses, trials, and weights, and signature, a summary of the likelihood used to check that candidates are comparable.

    • formula (as text), family, and link. NB2 and Gamma records add nuisance.

  • fits: NULL unless keep_fits = TRUE. Otherwise the full model of each fold, fitted to that fold's analysis rows only.

  • raster_groups: present only for inputs from kernel_prep_by_group(). For each fold, the map labels of the analysis and assessment rows. These are fixed inputs, not fitted random effects.

  • settings: list with family, link, backend ("glm" for cross_validate_glm() and "training_selection" for select_cv()), metrics, the control lists used, and labels that state what the scores mean. normalization = "training_only" and parameter_uncertainty = "not_integrated", for example, say that standardization came from the analysis rows and that the predictions treat fitted parameters as known. cv_tab() checks these labels before comparing candidates.

  • call: the matched call.

A select_cv() result also holds selection, with the criterion and ties rule, the candidates, the metrics kept and metrics_dropped, chosen (the candidate selected in each fold, NA when selection failed), tables (the training information-criterion table of each fold), candidate_settings, candidate_warnings, and candidate_diagnostics. Its settings$controls_from names the candidate whose controls fill the shared settings. NB2 and Gamma selections add settings$fold_settings, the settings of the model chosen in each fold.

Functions that read it

  • print() reports how many folds were scored and how many input rows were assessed, warns when the result is incomplete, and prints summary.

  • cv_tab() ranks complete results on one score, after checking that every candidate used identical folds, responses, trials, and weights.

  • select_cv() scores a rule that picks a model in each fold by its training AIC, AICc, or BIC. It needs selection_records or fits.

  • aic_tab() and bic_tab() refuse a cross-validation result, because held-out scores are not a maximized likelihood.

Conditional choice results (multiScaleR_choice_cv)

cross_validate_clogit() scores the probability of the used alternative within each held-out choice set, and the elements change accordingly.

  • predictions has one row per alternative. observed is 1 for the used alternative and 0 for the available ones, choice is the set ID, and trials and weight are 1. linear_predictor is uncentered, so only differences within a set matter. prediction is the probability of the alternative within its set (the probabilities of a set sum to 1), and log_probability is its natural log. Only the used alternative is eligible, and its neg_log_score is the negative log probability of the choice. Log scores are computed directly on the log scale, so they stay finite when a printed probability rounds to zero.

  • summary and metrics hold neg_log_score only, averaged over choice sets, with unit = "choice_set". n_assessment, n_scored, and weight_sum count sets, and n_alternatives counts the alternative rows. A model without covariates or offsets gives each of k alternatives a probability of 1/k and scores log(k), for example 1.099 for three alternatives.

  • fold_results counts alternative rows, and targets adds choice.

  • diagnostics holds initial and native (iteration count iter and partial-likelihood method) and scale.

  • selection_records are version 2. Their nobs counts choice sets (one event each), not alternatives, and they record the method.

  • settings gives family = "conditional_choice", link = "softmax", the method, and backend = "clogit" when no scales were estimated.

  • Its print() method reports the folds scored and prints summary.

Spatial field results (multiScaleR_field_cv)

cross_validate_field() scores each held-out block jointly, so that correlation among neighboring held-out observations counts.

  • predictions holds fold, row_id, observed, prediction (the predicted response mean), squared_error, absolute_error, and eligible, plus four variance columns. new_location_field_variance is the field variance that would remain even if the field were known exactly at the training locations, and fitted_training_field_variance is the extra variance that arises because the field there is itself estimated. Both are on the linear-predictor scale and, for non-Gaussian families, describe a local Gaussian approximation. observation_noise_variance (response scale) is the observation variance, averaged over the field for non-Gaussian families. observation_predictive_SE (response scale) is the standard deviation of a new observation, combining the field and the noise. It is a predictive SD, not the standard error of the mean.

  • joint_scores holds, for each fold, the block size n and the block's neg_log_score. Gaussian blocks add the quadratic loss and log_determinant. Laplace blocks add the analysis and combined log densities, their latent-mode diagnostics, and the gap from the native analysis likelihood.

  • summary has columns metric, estimate, n_assessment, unit, and complete. The log score is the sum of the block scores divided by the number of assessment observations, with unit "joint_block_density_per_observation" or "joint_block_mass_per_observation" (counts and 0/1 data). RMSE and MAE have unit "response". There is no metrics table, so use cv_tab(by_fold = TRUE) for fold scores.

  • training holds the analysis row_ids, parameters (field_SD, the correlation range in coordinate units, observation_SD or the NB2 or Gamma dispersion, and parameter counts), coefficients (link scale), and, with kernel inputs, normalization, scale_est, bin_reference, and the number of refits.

  • selection_records are always kept. Each holds logLik, K, native_K, ecological_K, nobs, training_ids, and hashes of the training responses and coordinates.

  • diagnostics holds the native fit record of each fold, including the covariance starts tried and the path of its audit file.

  • targets holds row_id and observed, coordinates holds row_id, x, and y, and integrity_sha256 is a hash of the recorded results. cv_tab() and select_cv() refuse a result whose records were changed after the run.

Mixed model results (multiScaleR_mixed_cv)

cross_validate_mixed() scores all held-out rows of a group jointly, because they share one unknown group effect.

  • predictions adds group, and prediction is the response mean integrated over the group effect (the success probability per trial for binomial data).

  • joint_scores holds, for each scored fold, a data frame with group, the number of held-out rows n, and the group's joint neg_log_score.

  • In summary and metrics, the log score is the sum of the group scores divided by the number of assessment rows (unit "joint_group_density_per_row"). RMSE and MAE have unit "response", or "proportion" for binomial data, where they compare the predicted probability with the observed fraction of successes. The Brier score has unit "trial".

  • training holds the analysis row_ids, coefficients (link scale), the random-effect covariance, the native dispersion (1 for Poisson and binomial), and any fitted scale_est, normalization, and bin_reference.

  • selection_records are always kept, with logLik, K, native_K, ecological_K, nobs, and the analysis row IDs.

  • diagnostics holds convergence, positive_hessian, native_message, and scale_convergence, and integrity_sha256 protects the records as for field results.

Bayesian results (multiScaleR_bayes_cv)

cross_validate_bayes() scores held-out blocks with the posterior predictive density, the only score in the package that averages over parameter uncertainty. Its summary reports the joint negative log score per observation, and its predictions hold posterior mean responses and marginal row scores. It has no training likelihood, so select_cv() does not apply. See cross_validate_bayes() for its elements.

See also

cross_validate(), cv_tab(), select_cv(), and vignette("v08-cross-validation", package = "multiScaleR").

Examples

data("landscape_counts")
data("surv_pts")
# Three spatial folds. The simulated coordinates are in meters.
folds <- spatial_cv_folds(crds(vect(surv_pts)), block_size = 1000, k = 3,
                          crs = 32617)
cv <- cross_validate_glm(counts ~ site, landscape_counts, folds,
                         family = "poisson", keep_selection = TRUE)
class(cv)
#> [1] "multiScaleR_cv"
cv$complete           # TRUE: every fold was fitted and scored
#> [1] TRUE
cv$summary            # pooled scores, one row per metric, lower is better
#>          metric estimate        unit n_assessment n_scored weight_sum complete
#> 1          rmse 2.232857 observation          100      100        100     TRUE
#> 2           mae 1.661678 observation          100      100        100     TRUE
#> 3 neg_log_score 2.169778 observation          100      100        100     TRUE
#> 4      deviance 2.372818 observation          100      100        100     TRUE
cv$metrics[cv$metrics$metric == "rmse", ]   # the same score in each fold
#>    fold metric estimate        unit n_assessment n_scored weight_sum complete
#> 1 fold1   rmse 2.091114 observation           34       34         34     TRUE
#> 5 fold2   rmse 1.620645 observation           33       33         33     TRUE
#> 9 fold3   rmse 2.824229 observation           33       33         33     TRUE
head(cv$predictions)  # one row per held-out observation, with its losses
#>    fold row_id observed trials prediction weight eligible      rmse       mae
#> 1 fold1      2        2      1   3.000225      1     TRUE 1.0004503 1.0002251
#> 2 fold1      5        2      1   2.946952      1     TRUE 0.8967175 0.9469517
#> 3 fold1      6        0      1   1.995418      1     TRUE 3.9816928 1.9954179
#> 4 fold1      8        1      1   1.690686      1     TRUE 0.4770469 0.6906858
#> 5 fold1     11        0      1   1.673290      1     TRUE 2.7998998 1.6732901
#> 6 fold1     26        1      1   2.537614      1     TRUE 2.3642583 1.5376145
#>   neg_log_score  deviance
#> 1      1.495998 0.3782897
#> 2      1.478556 0.3434069
#> 3      1.995418 3.9908359
#> 4      1.165552 0.3311031
#> 5      1.673290 3.3465802
#> 6      1.606390 1.2127800
cv$fold_results       # rows fitted and held out, and the status of each fold
#>    fold n_analysis n_assessment status
#> 1 fold1         66           34 scored
#> 2 fold2         67           33 scored
#> 3 fold3         67           33 scored
cv$training$fold1$coefficients   # log-link coefficients fitted in fold 1
#> (Intercept)        site 
#>   0.7447308   0.1776788 

# What select_cv() reads from each fold
cv$selection_records$fold1$data[c("logLik", "K", "nobs")]
#> $logLik
#> [1] -141.7151
#> 
#> $K
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $nobs
#> [1] 66
#> 

# The pooled RMSE is the square root of the mean squared error over all
# held-out rows, not the mean of the three fold RMSEs
sqrt(mean(cv$predictions$rmse))
#> [1] 2.232857
